name: Same-account direct IAM-user resource grant (suite-2 test 32)
note: IAM-1204 / acceptance-suite-2 test 32. An S3 bucket policy grants a named IAM user (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/Alice) in the resource-OWNING account (123456789012) permission to read the bucket's objects. Because S3 bucket/object ARNs carry NO account id, the owning account is supplied EXPLICITLY in the attached-resource context (the 'resource-policy context is explicit' invariant). With the owning account known and equal to the principal's account, this is a DIRECT SAME-ACCOUNT grant (RESOURCE-SAME-ACCOUNT-GRANT, medium), NOT cross-account and NOT public. The finding explains the resource-vs-identity evaluation distinction: within one account AWS unions identity + resource permissions, so an IMPLICIT deny in the user's identity policy / permissions boundary does not, by itself, limit this direct resource-policy grant; an applicable EXPLICIT deny still blocks. The user principal is typed distinctly (IAM user) and never generalized to a role or cross-account principal.
